subject: Geography
central_question: How do geomorphic agents erode, transport and deposit material to create and transform landforms through time?
in_scope_units: Running water: landscape stages, erosional and depositional landforms
Groundwater: karst topography, solution landforms, caves and cave deposits
Waves and currents: high rocky and low sedimentary coasts
Winds and sheet wash in deserts
banned_topics: Detailed internal earth structure and plate tectonic theory
Ocean-water wave mechanics, tides and currents as a separate oceanography topic
Groundwater as a water resource rather than as a geomorphic agent

known_pitfalls.claim: A meander is itself a depositional landform.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter explicitly calls a meander a channel pattern, not a landform in itself.

known_pitfalls.claim: Groundwater creates karst mainly by mechanical erosion.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mechanical removal is insignificant; solution and precipitation in limestone or dolomite produce karst landforms.

known_pitfalls.claim: Wind alone creates desert erosional landforms.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter also gives major roles to sheet floods, mass wasting and weathering.
Glacial till is unassorted, whereas glacio-fluvial outwash is roughly stratified and assorted.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 2(i): interpret incised meanders and alluvial-plain meanders
NCERT Exercise 2(ii): explain valley sinks or uvalas
NCERT Exercise 2(iv): locate and name glacial linear depositional forms
NCERT Exercise 2(v): explain wind action and other desert agents
NCERT Exercise 3(i): explain the dominance of running water
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1, 2 and 3 followed by Project Work on local landforms, materials and processes.
